newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher, Cerus shares rally.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher, Cerus shares rally.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Monday, buoyed by rising bond prices and favourable first-half company results, brokers said.
Shares in holding company Cerus rallied 12 percent after two suspensions, limit-up, on a newspaper report that it was negotiating a possible buyout by CGIP.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 13.10 points, or 0.65 percent, at 2,017.85 at 0900 GMT, while the CAC-40 September futures contract was 6.5 points higher at 2,023.
CGIP shares were down slightly on the report in Les Echos that said it was in buyout talks with Cerus chairman Carlo De Benedetti.
Cerus and CGIP declined to comment.
The report said such a deal would please French authorities and carmakers which want car parts manufacturer Valeo, in which Cerus holds a controlling 28 percent stake, to stay in French hands.
It would provide cash for De Benedetti's holdings CIR and Cofide.
Valeo shares were down as the report said the Cerus deal would be engineered to avoid a takeover bid for Valeo.
